name: All determination is negation
plain_explanation: Anything finite is defined by its limits - by what it is not - so nothing finite can be wholly real or positive; only an infinite, unbounded being can be completely positive.
precise_definition: Spinoza's principle that finite things are individuated by their boundaries (physical or logical), which are a form of negation, so that only the single absolutely infinite substance is wholly positive.
why_it_mattered: It is the pivot of Spinoza's argument for pantheism: since only one being can be wholly positive, and everything positive must belong to it, that being must be absolutely infinite and singular.
historical_origin: Spinoza's own formulation, built on the logic of subject and predicate that Russell says underlies his whole metaphysic.
